title: I Have No Tears to Shed
description: I Have No Tears to Shed in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), and this page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I have no tears to shed, For grief my soul hath none; My heart hath nev-er bled, For ought that I have done; I weep not when I hear Thee say That sin hath car-ried me a-way.

lines: I have no tears to shed,
For grief my soul hath none;
For ought that I have done;
I weep not when I hear Thee say
That sin hath carried me away.
I have no tears to shed;
Wilt Thou not touch my heart,
And bid sin's wounds run red,
Then shall I lift my prayer and say,
For Thou, O Lord, dost will
That all should seek Thy face,
Who ever sought Thy love in vain,
Or failed Thy pardon to obtain?

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
